decision: done = baseline below 100, zig build test green after each commit, each residue site has a reason in issue 02
inventory: 391 drops. 121 catch-blocks (97 in presentation, 63 set .out_of_memory), 100 value fallbacks (51 render), 43 other returns, 30 return error.X, 21 catch {}, 13 catch unreachable, 10 else
why: size the run before designing it

decision: compiler-driven codemod: rewrite catch H to catch |err| switch (err) {}, read 'unhandled error value' notes, write the names as one prong with H as body, loop until no site is pending
why: the compiler knows each callee error set; listing them by hand is slow and wrong; an exhaustive prong with the same body keeps behavior identical
evidence: probe: zig test on empty switch printed note: unhandled error value: 'error.OutOfMemory'

decision: a site never reported by the compiler, or with more than 3 names, or with an anyerror callee, or a shadowed capture, goes back to its old text and joins the residue
why: an unanalyzed empty switch is noreturn and would change behavior; a large set is a real drop to review, not to launder
evidence: zig reports one error per function per run

decision: a handler that sets .out_of_memory but whose callee also returns a non-OOM error is reverted and listed as a mislabel bug
why: do not hide a wrong label behind a checked switch

decision: PRD Q1: OOM in a scratch render path is an expected outcome; drop it through a named OutOfMemory prong, no record
why: the fallback label is a valid state and a record would repeat every frame

decision: PRD Q2: a log-only catch that records the cause is not a ratchet drop; the residue review asks whether the handler leaves a valid state
why: the ratchet counts lost causes; state validity needs a human reading
all groups share presentation.zig and one global compile loop

decision: allocPrint catch "" in render.zig goes behind one helper first, as the issue proposes
render.zig formatLabel helper holds the OOM switch; 71 allocPrint(scratch) label sites migrated
why: issue 02 group 1; fallbacks are literals or pure reads already formatted, so eager evaluation is safe
evidence: zig build test exit 0; check_diagnostics render.zig 92->21

decision: pending form is catch |err| if (false) H else switch (err) {} instead of a bare empty switch
why: the dead branch keeps every name of H referenced, so AstGen raises no unused or never-mutated local error that would stall a whole file
evidence: probe p.zig: if (false) branch skipped by Sema, switch still reports unhandled notes

decision: analysis via check_build.zig wrapper: every unfiltered exe/test Compile step of build.zig copied without getEmittedBin, so -fno-emit-bin
why: covers bbr, bbr-bench, file-acquisition and buffer-search benches, mod/exe tests, core-linux-tests, grammar-cli-integration without running benches or tests
evidence: 6 s incremental vs 3 min zig build test
